channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Bishkek Residents May Receive Loans for Heat Pump Installation
item.description: A meeting in Bishkek discussed a World Bank project to improve air quality in Kyrgyzstan. A key focus is a credit line for households to install heat pumps, enhancing energy efficiency and reducing emissions during the heating season.

item.title: Uzbekistan and South Korea deepen strategic partnership amid global shifts
item.description: Uzbekistan and South Korea are strengthening their strategic partnership, expanding cooperation beyond trade and investment to encompass industrial cooperation. This collaboration is gaining importance amid global geopolitical changes and economic transformations, with Central Asia seen as a promising region for diversification and high-tech development.

item.title: Uzbekistan shifts environmental control from reactive to proactive approach
item.description: Uzbekistan is transforming its environmental oversight from a reactive tool to a proactive system, focusing on risk prediction and impact assessment during planning. The "On Environmental Control" law emphasizes prevention alongside enforcement, reflecting a global shift towards risk-oriented and partner-based supervision.

item.title: Navoiy region develops agriculture through land reclamation and irrigation projects
item.description: The Kanimekh district in Uzbekistan's Navoiy region is developing agriculture by reclaiming abandoned pastures and improving irrigation. Projects include the Kengsoy canal to water 3,800 hectares and a reservoir for 1.6 million cubic meters. Investment is being attracted for crop and livestock feed production.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan establishes registry for waste recycling companies
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is creating a digital registry of waste recyclers to promote a circular economy and extended producer responsibility. The Ministry of Natural Resources is licensing and supporting companies that process cardboard, plastic, textiles, and polymer bags into new raw materials or products for domestic use and export.

item.title: Russia to halt gas exports to Armenia citing maintenance, impacting relations
item.description: Russia will suspend gas exports to Armenia starting September 15 due to maintenance. Armenia will rely on Iranian gas and domestic reserves. This decision comes amid deteriorating political and economic relations between the two countries.

item.title: Uzbekistan and South Korea sign 13 agreements on transport, AI, and intellectual property
item.description: Uzbekistan and South Korea exchanged documents on expanding trade, economic, investment, and humanitarian cooperation. Thirteen interdepartmental agreements and memorandums were signed, covering sectors like transport, AI, agriculture, and intellectual property protection.

item.title: Uzbekistan significantly increases liquefied petroleum gas imports amid rising global prices
item.description: Uzbekistan has sharply increased its imports of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), known as propane. The cost of purchasing this gas from abroad has significantly risen, impacting the domestic market. This trend reflects a growing demand or supply challenges in the international LPG market.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to install 44,000 smart electricity meters in Toktogul and Nooken districts
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Jalal-Abad Electric Network Enterprise is installing automated systems for commercial electricity accounting. By 2026, 44,000 smart meters will be installed in the Toktogul and Nooken districts. The Ministry of Energy reports 106,000 such meters were installed in the region since 2024. Installation is free for consumers.

item.title: South Korean Ambassador discusses enhanced practical cooperation with Uzbekistan
item.description: South Korean Ambassador Won Do-yeon highlighted the deepening relationship between South Korea and Uzbekistan, emphasizing practical cooperation. He noted South Korea's appreciation for President Mirziyoyev's policies promoting regional stability and cooperation in Central Asia. The upcoming first Central Asia-Republic of Korea summit in Seoul is expected to yield significant practical outcomes.

item.title: Russia expelled over 72,000 migrants in six months, denied entry to 7,700
item.description: In the first half of the year, Russia expelled more than 72,000 migrants from its territory. Additionally, entry was denied to another 7,700 foreign nationals. Further details are available.

item.title: German journalist uncovered Russian agents in Germany using a fake account
item.description: A German journalist, posing as 'Katya' on a fake social media account, exposed how Russian agents operate covertly in Germany. The journalist gained the trust of Russian operatives by expressing admiration for Putin online, subsequently receiving assignments from them.

item.title: Eurasian Economic Commission Eases Import Rules for Tomatoes, Peppers, and Eggplants
item.description: The Eurasian Economic Commission has amended quarantine phytosanitary requirements for the Eurasian Economic Union. The changes remove the need for certificates confirming the absence of Pepino mosaic virus in fresh or chilled tomatoes, peppers, and eggplants. Requirements for seed and planting material remain. This aims to reduce administrative burdens and improve trade conditions for these vegetables.

item.title: Uzbekistan Establishes Reserve Formation Rules for Potential Bank Asset Losses
item.description: Uzbekistan has set regulations for creating reserves against potential losses from bank assets. These assets will be categorized into five groups, with reserve rates ranging from 1% to 100%.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Foreign Trade Reaches $10 Billion in January-July 2026
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's foreign trade turnover hit $10 billion from January to July 2026, a 7.7% increase year-on-year. Exports grew 2.7% to $1.66 billion, while imports rose 8.7% to $8.34 billion, maintaining Kyrgyzstan's reliance on imports.

item.title: Uzbekistan: 133 of 238 SSPE-afflicted children unvaccinated against measles, says Health Ministry
item.description: Uzbekistan's Health Ministry reported that 133 out of 238 children diagnosed with Subacute Sclerosing Panencephalitis (SSPE) have not received the measles vaccine. Parents of these children gathered to request medication, medical aid, and financial support. SSPE is a fatal disease caused by the measles virus, leading to irreversible brain damage.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's economic growth reached 11 percent in eight months, says cabinet head
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's economy grew by 11 percent in the first eight months of the year, reaching 1.397 trillion soms, according to cabinet head Adylbek Kasymaliev. Investments in fixed capital increased by 61.2%, construction by 61%, industrial production by 8.8%, and agriculture by 6.4%.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Pakistan Sign Agreement to Boost Freight Transit
item.description: Kyrgyzstan and Pakistan have approved an agreement to expand transit trade, aiming to enhance Kyrgyzstan's integration into international transport corridors. The deal facilitates road, rail, and air transport to Pakistani seaports like Karachi, Qasim, and Gwadar, and includes infrastructure development.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Secures Up to $50 Million Grant for Green Energy Transition
item.description: Kyrgyzstan may receive up to $50 million in grant financing from the International Development Association for the iFIRST project, aimed at reducing greenhouse gas emissions and improving energy efficiency. The project seeks to establish a carbon financing system and support energy reforms.

item.title: Uzbek President Discusses Bilateral Relations and Cooperation with South Korea
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev gave an interview to 'The Korea Herald' discussing Uzbek-Korean relations, high-tech cooperation, investments, and regional partnerships. He noted a fivefold increase in trade and over $8 billion in Korean investments, highlighting future cooperation in AI, critical minerals, and smart cities.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Dollar Exchange Rate Decreases for Fourth Consecutive Day
item.description: The dollar exchange rate in Uzbekistan has fallen for the fourth day in a row. The Central Bank announced the official exchange rates for foreign currencies against the Uzbek soum, effective September 15.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Bulgaria Enter New Phase of Cooperation
item.description: Uzbekistan and Bulgaria are entering a new phase of cooperation 34 years after establishing diplomatic relations. The countries aim to deepen political dialogue and expand trade-economic ties, building on agreements signed during the Bulgarian President's visit.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and China to build 56-meter bridge at Bedel border crossing
item.description: A permanent 56-meter road bridge will be constructed across the Uzongu-Kuush River near the Bedel checkpoint on the Kyrgyz-Chinese border. The bridge aims to develop transport links and improve checkpoint infrastructure. Kyrgyzstan and China will each finance their respective halves of the bridge and access roads. The estimated cost is approximately $940,000.

item.title: Russia's revenue from migrants increased, crime decreased in first half of year
item.description: Labor migrants contributed 321 billion rubles (approximately $4 billion) to Russia's budget in the first six months of the year, a 30% increase from the previous year. Russian authorities also reported a 40% decrease in crimes committed by foreign citizens during the same period. This comes amid tightened migration policies in Russia.

item.title: NGMK transitions from digitalization to intelligent production with AI focus
item.description: The Navoi Mining and Metallurgical Combinat (NGMK) is advancing its digital transformation, moving towards intelligent production incorporating artificial intelligence. A seminar, co-organized with the Ministry of Mining and Geology, focused on practical applications of digital solutions and AI for forecasting and optimizing production processes.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov to visit South Korea for official talks and summit
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov will make an official visit to South Korea from September 15-18 at the invitation of President Lee Jae Myung. He will attend the first Central Asia-Republic of Korea summit, participate in bilateral talks, and witness the signing of economic and investment agreements.

item.title: Uzbekistan proposes to calculate child support based on children's needs, not parental income
item.description: Uzbekistan is considering changing child support calculations to focus on children's needs rather than parental income. The proposal aims to ensure children receive adequate support by establishing a minimum consumer basket based on age. This would prevent parents from reducing payments by hiding income or taking low-paying jobs.

item.title: Uzbek President outlines five priority areas for economic cooperation with South Korea
item.description: During his visit, President Shavkat Mirziyoyev identified five priority areas for economic cooperation with South Korea. Prospective projects worth nearly $12 billion have been prepared. Additionally, a Strategic Partnership Program with Korea Eximbank valued at $8 billion was adopted.

item.title: Uzbekistan and South Korea Expand Cooperation in Critical Minerals and Technology
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev held talks with South Korean President Lee Jae-myung in Seoul, focusing on strengthening the special strategic partnership. Both leaders noted the growth in trade and investment, with over 700 joint ventures in Uzbekistan. Cooperation will expand in sectors like healthcare, industry, energy, and education.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Accounts Chamber finds $25 million loan to Alfa Oil ineffective
item.description: An Accounts Chamber auditor stated that a $25 million loan provided to Alfa Oil LLC in 2025 to curb fuel prices was ineffective. The loan, with a 7% interest rate covered by the state, only accounted for 12-13% of the market's fuel supply. The auditor criticized the loan's terms and lack of broad market impact.

item.title: Winners announced for energy sector sports competition "TES Cup"
item.description: Over 200 employees from thermal power plants across the country participated in the "TES Cup" sports competition, organized under the motto "One team, one goal, one victory!" Winners received diplomas, medals, and gifts.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's foreign trade reaches $10 billion in January-July 2026
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's foreign trade volume reached $10 billion in January-July 2026, a 7.7% increase from the same period in 2025. Exports grew by 2.7% to $1.66 billion, while imports rose by 8.7% to $8.34 billion. The trade deficit widened by $906.2 million in July.

item.title: Three children of Uzbek women imprisoned in Russia returned to Uzbekistan
item.description: The underage children of Uzbek women held in penal institutions in Russia's Mordovia and Samara regions have been returned to Uzbekistan. Consular officials facilitated the repatriation process, ensuring all legal procedures were completed.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Pakistan to open new cargo transit route
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's parliament committee approved an agreement with Pakistan to expand transit trade. The deal aims to enhance Kyrgyzstan's transit potential and integration into international transport corridors, creating a legal framework for carriers on the Kyrgyzstan-China-Pakistan route. It allows for alternative routes using road, rail, and air transport to Pakistani seaports.

item.title: Tajikistan and UNICEF discuss cooperation on environmental programs
item.description: Tajikistan's Committee for Environmental Protection met with the newly appointed UNICEF Representative to Tajikistan, Gabriella Akimova. They discussed cooperation on environmental protection programs aligned with the National Development Strategy until 2030 and priorities for the 2027 Joint Work Plan. Key areas include climate change, environmental safety, and ecological literacy for youth.

item.title: Uzbekistan's exports decrease by 3.6% in seven months, gold sales decline impacts total revenue
item.description: Uzbekistan's exports fell by 3.6% in the first seven months of the year, primarily due to a reduction in gold sales, which affected overall export revenues. Imports, however, saw an increase of approximately 18% during the same period. Detailed figures are available via the provided link.

item.title: South Korea and Central Asia Launch C5+1 Industrial Cooperation
item.description: South Korea and five Central Asian nations agreed to expand industrial cooperation, trade, and supply chains. Priority areas include trade development, industrial parks, strategic minerals like lithium, advanced technologies, and training specialists. The C5+1 format aims to be a platform for joint projects and economic ties.

item.title: Uzbek Citizen Injured in Drone Attack in Russia Repatriated
item.description: An Uzbek citizen severely injured in a drone attack in Nizhnekamsk, Russia, was brought back to Uzbekistan on September 13. The decision to repatriate was made after his condition stabilized and Russian doctors permitted evacuation. He is continuing treatment and rehabilitation in Uzbekistan.

item.title: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev Officially Welcomed in Seoul
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev received an official welcome ceremony at the South Korean presidential residence on September 14. President Mirziyoyev and his wife were greeted by President Yoon Suk Yeol and his wife. The ceremony included an honor guard and national anthems, followed by high-level talks.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Debt to China Revealed; Repayment Possible Now, Says Deputy Finance Minister
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's debt to China has been disclosed, with the Deputy Finance Minister stating it can be repaid immediately. However, he recommended a phased approach. The exact amount of the debt was not specified in the report.
